title: Marriage License (Historical)

origin.publisher: Library of Congress, Prints and Photographs Division (Bain News Service glass negative), via Wikimedia Commons
origin.title: Taft Marriage License, Ohio (photographed between ca. 1910 and ca. 1915)
origin.clearance_note: A Bain News Service glass-plate photograph of the 1886 Hamilton County, Ohio marriage license of William Howard Taft and Helen Louise Herron, held by the Library of Congress (Flickr ID 2162683291) with 'no known restrictions on publication' and hosted on Wikimedia Commons. Downloaded by script from Commons as a 1024x751 greyscale JPEG and wrapped in a one-page PDF with no metadata. Published as printed under the historical-record and public-figure exemptions. Evidence: the record is dated June 19, 1886 on its face, more than 72 years ago; William Howard Taft, 27th President of the United States, died March 8, 1930, and Helen Herron Taft died May 22, 1943 (Encyclopaedia Britannica: britannica.com/biography/William-Howard-Taft and britannica.com/biography/Helen-Taft). The probate judge, deputy clerk and officiant appear in their official roles.

notes: The request asked for the photograph to be used as is; it was, unredacted, under the historical-record and public-figure exemptions with the evidence in clearance_note. No feature page or fields were requested. The overlay follows the license from issue to return: its number, the two people named in the sworn affidavit, the probate judge who granted it, and the officiant's line in the marriage return. Named individuals are featured because they are the substance of a marriage license and here they are a president and first lady, both long deceased. The dates ground OFF only because the schema normalizes them to YYYY-MM-DD.
